task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: opponent next-possession points per possession after play type X
AVOID label thresholds for play types
own-sequence lagged effects of play types
derived possession records from play-by-play graph database
methodological_questions: Is the opponent next-possession PPP after play X large enough to justify an AVOID label, and what threshold defines AVOID?
Can play-type labels be assigned reliably enough from the per-game files to support PPP comparisons?
Do points-on-possession labels create circular or lookahead leakage when the label is derived from the same outcome being tested?
Are own-sequence lag effects distinguishable from base-rate, foul-ending and score-context effects?
What multiplicity and placebo controls are needed across play types and lags?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type labeling audit of OTHER/DRIVE foul leakage. OTHER: 36% of possessions end in fouls, with PPP inflated (FOUL_BUCKET). DRIVE: 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK). PNR shows a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type. Recorded failure mechanism: C_artifact. Validation status: no_validation_recorded (evidence NOT_RECORDED). Verdict recorded as artifact_found.

Sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock (8/8 PTs). Recorded hypothesis: after the opponent runs play type X, the next offensive play type Y scores above Y's unconditional H2 baseline, and every PT has a defensive aftershock. Recorded result: the aftershock replicated in all 8 play types for all games and playoffs (for example CUT +0.119, n=21,398 all games; +0.131, n=1,145 playoffs). Top pair premium recorded as PUTBACK to TRANSITION +0.084, n=565. Recorded limitation: [prior work]. Failure mechanism: D_positive (no failure).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Defining play-type PPP comparisons from the initiation_type mapping of the play-by-play (labels assigned from the per-game action fields).
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a C_artifact: the mapping covered only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%), OTHER PPP was inflated by 36% foul endings, DRIVE sat 12pp below the foul benchmark, and no validation was recorded. The apparent play-type efficiency differences were judged artifacts of labeling and foul endings rather than real efficiency.

evidence_establishes: Within the earlier project work, a play-type labeling derived from initiation_type was found to be unreliable: it covers under 1% of possessions in the audited check and its PPP differences were attributed to foul-ending contamination.
Foul endings are a recorded source of PPP inflation for at least the OTHER and PNR categories, so any PPP-by-play-type comparison needs foul-ending control.

A defensive aftershock pattern after play-type success was recorded as supported across all 8 play types in the all-games and playoff samples (FAM:[prior work]), with recorded limitation [prior work].
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record measures opponent next-possession PPP specifically after play X with an AVOID threshold; FAM:[prior work] concerns a defensive aftershock and a sequential offensive pair premium, which is related but not the same estimand.
No retrieved record establishes a validated AVOID threshold or its operating characteristics.
No retrieved record establishes whether own-sequence lag effects survive foul, base-rate and score-context controls.
The FAM:[prior work] excerpt is truncated and its units and estimand definitions are not fully stated in the returned text; the full record was not read.
Whether the 2025-26 playoff data (partial before 2026-06-21) would change any result is not addressed.
own_inferences: The FAM:[prior work] aftershock result, even if supported, is measured on a play-type label set that [prior work][prior work] found to cover only 0.7% of possessions in its check. Its reliability depends on which labeling source it used, which the excerpt does not state.

Because AVOID labels are presumably built from opponent PPP after X, and the label construction uses the same points outcome, any AVOID label carries outcome-derived circularity unless the labeling and outcome windows are separated.

The foul-ending inflation recorded for OTHER and PNR implies that unadjusted opponent next-possession PPP will be biased upward for play types with high foul rates, which could produce spurious AVOID labels.
A sound test needs a label source validated for coverage and accuracy before any PPP comparison is run.
uncertainties: The exact AVOID threshold and its definition are not stated in the task or in any retrieved record.
The labeling source and coverage used in FAM:[prior work] are not stated in the returned excerpt.
[prior work][prior work] recorded no validation (NOT_RECORDED), so it is unknown whether a corrected labeling pipeline exists.
Per-play-type sample sizes for opponent next-possession outcomes, after restricting to complete regular-season and playoff data, are not known.
Whether the 2025-26 playoff data will be complete at the time of analysis is not known beyond the stated 2026-06-21 completion date, which is after the 2026-06-19 question date.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved [prior work][prior work] record shows that play-type labels from initiation_type cover 0.7% of possessions and produce foul-driven PPP artifacts, so the play-type measurement that the question depends on is not currently valid. This blocks a direct test. FAM:[prior work] is supported and related, but it does not answer the opponent next-possession AVOID question and carries a small-sample limitation. Together these changed the decision from a direct test to do_not_proceed until the labeling is validated.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels from initiation_type cover only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) in the earlier audit, so play-type-specific opponent next-possession PPP cannot be estimated from the current labels without a validated labeling source.
Foul endings inflate PPP for OTHER (36%) and PNR (22% foul rate) and distort DRIVE, so unadjusted play-type PPP differences conflate efficiency with foul-ending mechanics.
AVOID labels built from the points outcome of the same possessions being evaluated create circularity unless labeling and outcome windows are separated.
The supporting aftershock record was flagged [prior work], and per-play-type next-possession samples after label restriction may be too small for stable AVOID thresholds.
Testing many play types across own-sequence and opponent lags inflates false-positive AVOID labels without correction.

prior_work.summary: FAM:[prior work] (supported, limited by small sample) addresses a related sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock after play-type success, which partly overlaps the question of opponent response after play X. [prior work][prior work] (artifact) shows that play-type labels from initiation_type are unreliable and foul-contaminated. Neither record answers the specific question of whether opponent next-possession PPP after play X justifies AVOID labels, and no retrieved record sets an AVOID threshold.

risks.text: Labels from initiation_type cover 0.7% of possessions and were recorded as producing artifacts; any label source must be validated for coverage and accuracy first.
Foul endings (OTHER 36%, PNR 22%) and score context can produce play-type PPP differences unrelated to efficiency.
Using the outcome points to define play-type AVOID labels and then testing opponent PPP on the same possessions is circular.
Labels that use information from the opponent's next possession, or post-play events, would leak the outcome into the predictor.
Per-play-type opponent next-possession samples may be too small for reliable AVOID thresholds, as flagged in FAM:[prior work] ([prior work]).
Rare play types and lags may have very few occurrences per team or game, making estimates unstable.
PPP per play type and lag has unknown split-half reliability across seasons and playoff versus regular season.
Many play types times own and opponent lags times AVOID thresholds inflate false positives.
Without placebo lags or shuffled labels, an observed opponent effect cannot be separated from base-rate or selection structure.
Play-type frequencies and efficiency change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooled estimates may mix regimes.

design.estimand: Within each validated play type X, the difference in the opponent's next-possession points per possession after X compared with a matched base-rate baseline (same period, score margin, clock, and foul-ending-adjusted expected PPP), at lags 0 and +1 for the opponent and own sequence, with lag -1 as a placebo. The AVOID threshold must be fixed before analysis.
design.unit: Offensive possession of team A, paired with the opponent's next possession, with the play-type label derived only from events before the possession's outcome window.
design.sample: Regular season 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs 2022-23 through 2024-25 only. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs unless complete (complete from 2026-06-21, after the question date). Include only play types with a validated labeling source covering a pre-specified minimum share of possessions.
design.power: Before analysis, compute per-play-type standard errors via game-clustered bootstrap, and require enough possessions per play type to detect the pre-registered minimum effect with the target power. The minimum effect and power level must be fixed in advance; they are not stated in [prior work] and are left as project decisions.
design.controls: Validate the play-type labeling source first (coverage and accuracy audit, benchmarking against foul-ending share as in [prior work][prior work]). Exclude or adjust for foul-ending possessions. Adjust for period, clock, score margin, team and opponent strength, and possession context. Use game-level clustering. Separate label windows from outcome windows to avoid outcome-derived labels.
design.falsification: Placebo tests: lag -1 opponent PPP, label shuffling within game, and team-randomized labels. The AVOID claim fails if the placebo distribution produces effects of similar size. Also test whether the effect survives after foul-ending adjustment.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary contrast (the AVOID threshold on opponent lag +1 for a single named play type set) and apply Benjamini-Hochberg control across play types and lags for secondary contrasts.
design.decision_rule: Claim an AVOID label only if (a) the labeling audit passes its pre-registered coverage and accuracy thresholds, (b) the primary contrast exceeds the pre-registered threshold with a confidence interval that excludes zero after multiplicity correction, and (c) the effect exceeds the placebo distribution and survives the foul-ending adjustment. Otherwise report as uncertain or artifact.
design.data_version: Freeze the 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, and the 2025-26 regular season from its 2026-04-13 completion. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs until complete (from 2026-06-21). Record the play-by-play version and the labeling pipeline version.
